ldap.admin-group.help: Users in this LDAP group will be assigned the admin role. Leave empty to manage roles manually.
ldap.attribute-mapping.desc: Map LDAP attributes to user fields
ldap.auth-mode.internal-ldap.desc: Users can log in with either local credentials or LDAP. Local auth is tried first, then LDAP as fallback.
ldap.auth-mode.internal.desc: Only local username/password authentication. LDAP is completely disabled.
ldap.auth-mode.ldap-only.desc: Only LDAP authentication is allowed. Local passwords are ignored. Make sure at least one LDAP admin user exists!
ldap.auto-create-user.help: Automatically create a local user account when an LDAP user logs in for the first time.
ldap.base-dn.help: Base distinguished name for user search. For LLDAP: ou=people,dc=example,dc=com
ldap.bind-credentials.desc: Service account used to search the LDAP directory. Leave empty for direct bind mode.
ldap.bind-dn.help: Distinguished Name of the service account. For LLDAP: uid=admin,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com
ldap.connection-settings.desc: Configure the connection to your LDAP server
ldap.connection-status.desc: Live connection status to your LDAP server
ldap.group-role-mapping.desc: Optionally map LDAP groups to NPM admin role
ldap.host.help: Hostname or IP address of the LDAP server. Leave empty if using a full URL below.
ldap.multi-server.desc: Add multiple LDAP servers for high availability. If configured, these override the single host/URL above. Servers are tried in priority order (lower number = higher priority).
ldap.multi-server.label: Label
ldap.search-filter.help: LDAP search filter. '{{USERNAME}}' is replaced with the login username. For Active Directory: (sAMAccountName='{{USERNAME}}'). For LLDAP: (|(uid='{{USERNAME}}')(mail='{{USERNAME}}'))
ldap.search-settings.desc: Configure how users are found in the LDAP directory
ldap.sso.admin-emails.help: Comma-separated list of email addresses that should always receive admin role via SSO. These users are promoted to admin on every SSO login, regardless of Remote-Groups.
ldap.sso.desc: Enable Single Sign-On via trusted reverse proxy headers (e.g. Authelia, Authentik, Keycloak). When enabled, users authenticated by your reverse proxy are automatically logged in.
ldap.sso.enable.help: When enabled, the login page will check for Remote-Email / Remote-User / Remote-Name headers set by your reverse proxy (e.g. Authelia) and automatically log users in. Users are auto-created if they don't exist. 2FA is skipped for SSO users.
ldap.sso.header.groups: Comma-separated groups (optional, used for admin role mapping)
ldap.sso.header.name: Display name (optional)
ldap.sso.logout-url.help: When a user logs out of NPM, they will be redirected to this URL to also end their SSO session (e.g. Authelia, Authentik, Keycloak logout endpoint).
ldap.sso.setup-desc: Your reverse proxy must be configured to set the following headers when forwarding requests to NPM:
ldap.starttls.help: Upgrade connection to TLS using STARTTLS extension
ldap.sync-admin-group: Sync admin role on every login
ldap.sync-admin-group.help: When enabled, the admin role is granted/revoked on each login based on LDAP group membership.
ldap.timeouts.desc: Connection and search timeout settings (in milliseconds)
ldap.title: LDAP Authentication
ldap.tls-verify.help: Disable for self-signed certificates (not recommended for production)
ldap.url.help: Full LDAP URL. Use ldaps:// for SSL/TLS. Overrides host and port if set.
ldap.user-dn-template: User DN Template (for direct bind, optional)
ldap.user-dn-template.help: Template for constructing the user DN directly. '{{USERNAME}}' will be replaced. Used when no service account is configured.
ldap.user-sync.desc: Manually sync all LDAP users into Better NPM. New users will be created, existing users will be updated.
